title: Compound interest and the number e

learn.title: Interest on interest
learn.body: With compound interest the bank adds interest to your balance, and the next interest is earned on the bigger amount. With principal $P$, yearly rate $r$ (as a decimal), $n$ compoundings per year and $t$ years: $A=P\left(1+\frac{r}{n}\right)^{nt}$.

learn.title: 1000 dollars at 6% for 5 years
steps: More frequent compounding earns a little more

learn.title: The number e
learn.body: Let $n$ grow very large, so interest is added continuously. Then $\left(1+\frac{1}{n}\right)^n$ settles near $e\approx 2.71828$. For continuous growth, $A=Pe^{rt}$. 1000 dollars at 6% for 5 years becomes $1000e^{0.3}\approx 1349.86$.
Continuous compounding is the limit. No matter how often you compound, you cannot beat $Pe^{rt}$.

questions.prompt: 1000 dollars at 4% compounded yearly for 2 years. What is the amount in dollars?
500 dollars at 10% compounded yearly for 1 year gives how many dollars?
What is $n$ when interest is compounded quarterly?

questions.explanation: Yearly gives 1338.23, monthly gives 1348.85 and continuous gives 1349.86.
$e$ is about 2.718. The value 3.141 is $\pi$ and 1.414 is $\sqrt{2}$.
Any nonzero base to the power 0 is 1.
